newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia jails top general linked to massacre.
newsitem.headline: Colombia jails top general linked to massacre.

text.p: A retired three-star general was arrested in Bogota on Friday after returning from a military academy in the United States to answer charges about his links to a massacre, judicial officials said.

An arrest warrant was issued for Gen. Farouk Yanine Diaz on July 25 on charges of involvement in the 1987 massacre of 19 merchants in Colombia's northwest Magdalena Medio region while serving as army commander in Santander province.

Yanine, who retired from the Colombian army three years ago, is an adviser on military and legal matters at the Interamerican Defence College in Washington -- an academy sponsored by the Organisation of American States whose goals include promoting human rights in Latin America.

His arrest on Friday marked the first time such a high-ranking officer, considered a hero by many colleagues for his successes in fighting leftist guerrillas, has been officially linked to the paramilitary groups that have killed with impunity across Colombia for years.

The Magdalena Medio slaughter was carried out by such a group. Alfonso de Jesus Baquero, currently serving 30 years for the massacre, recently testified that Yanine knew about the killings in advance and allowed them to happen. He also alleged Yanine was involved in organising paramilitary groups.
A report entitled State Terrorism in Colombia, drafted by human rights and church groups in 1992, accuses Yanine of a longstanding relationship with paramilitary groups.

Among other crimes, it alleges he ordered the torture-murders of three women, two brothers and a child in Santander province in 1984 and sanctioned the killing of a town mayor in the same province three years later.

Yanine, who spent 36 years in the army, was jailed at a military base after presenting himself for questioning at the prosecutor-general's office. His father, a Palestinian immigrant, is said to have fought beside Lawrence of Arabia.
